messages:
maya: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated (acct: acme-inc) saw a sudden spike of 429s during a short traffic burst this morning. They have Reserved Pool X attached, SLA says 99.9% for p95 latency and no sustained 429s. Tickets show a ~40s window with 5-10% 429s across requests.

alex: Can you paste the exact error headers and a short repro curl? Also which model and route?

maya: Route: /v1/generate -> model: redwood/opt-8b@v2, pool: reserved-pool-eu-02, token: scoped. Repro curl attached:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/opt-8b@v2","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":512}'
```

maya: Sample response headers we captured: ``x-rw-rate-limited: 1``, ``x-rw-rl-reason: reserved_pool_exhausted``, ``x-rw-pool-usage: 0.94``, ``x-rw-account-qps: 120``, ``x-rw-pool-capacity-qps: 128``

luis: Interesting — pool usage at 94% but pool cap 128 qps, account qps 120. That shouldn't produce 429s unless there's a per-route smoothing or a short-term burst window that exhausted tokens. Any burst shaping configured on the route?

maya: Not on the customer's config (they use default smoothing). Console shows autoscale enabled but no active scaling events coincident with the spike. No other tenants reported issues in eu-02.

priya: Quick checklist: 1) confirm token-bucket burst size and refill interval for reserved pools 2) check if any soft headroom (safety cushion) kicked in 3) look for fallback logic routing to cheaper variant that might have different capacity.

alex: I pulled the allocator logs for pool eu-02 around the window. Saw short-lived worker restarts (~3 workers) due to OOM on a quantized path at 10:13:22 -> 10:13:31 UTC. Autoscaler did not add nodes until ~10:13:45. That 14s gap could create a transient deficit. I also see a note: "apply_headroom_policy: true" in the pool config for that tenant which applies a conservative per-account cap when worker churn occurs.

maya: That aligns with customer timeline. They reported first 429s at 10:13:24. Any idea why autoscaler lagged?

luis: Likely the scaler cooldown or backoff policy. Default scale-up delay can be 20s if we've been scaling recently. But a restart-induced capacity drop should trigger immediate ephemeral burst handling — unless headroom policy prevents temporary overcommit to maintain latency SLOs.

priya: Can we confirm which policy tripped? Run:
```
select * from allocations where pool = 'reserved-pool-eu-02' and ts between 1715000000 and 1715010000;
```
and check fields: active_workers, queued_requests, headroom_applied, scale_action.

alex: I ran that and pasted snippets:
```
10:13:20 active_workers=24 queued_requests=12 headroom_applied=true scale_action=none
10:13:30 active_workers=21 queued_requests=48 headroom_applied=true scale_action=scale_up_pending
10:13:45 active_workers=25 queued_requests=2 headroom_applied=false scale_action=scale_up
```

alex: So during 10:13:30 we were -3 workers, queued spiked, headroom applied prevented immediate serving beyond per-account cap -> 429s. Scale action queued and completed ~15s later.

maya: Customer wants to understand: why headroom applies at 94% usage and how to avoid 429s for short bursts. Also they're worried about SLA credit.

luis: Explanation: headroom policy multilayer: when worker churn or OOMs occur, the allocator toggles a conservative mode that reduces effective pool capacity for fairness and latency preservation. It uses a rolling average and a safety margin. Short-term bursts can be absorbed if bucket burst_size >= request burst, otherwise you'll see immediate 429s during the deficit window.

priya: Options to recommend to customer: 1) increase reserved-pool min_workers (prevent scaling below threshold) 2) tune per-account burst allowance (increase token-bucket burst_size) 3) enable proactive warm-up (pre-scale on known deploys) 4) use dedicated fallback model variant with lower memory to avoid OOMs.

maya: Customer also asked for repro steps we ran. Can we provide a minimal load script they can run to reproduce locally? I made a simple k6 snippet that ramps from 20 -> 200 rps over 30s against their route; linked logs show 429 onset when worker count dipped.

alex: I'll draft a support reply with: timeline, allocator excerpts, OOM evidence, the k6 repro, and recommended mitigations. Also propose a one-off exception to billing SLA while we confirm mitigation — flag for finance.

deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-4891 reserved-pool-eu-02 transient-429s. Assigned: luis, alex.

maya: Thanks — I'll loop in the customer and ask if they'd like us to apply a temporary increase to their pool min_workers while we root cause the OOMs.

luis: Also filing infra bug to track quantized path OOMs on opt-8b v2. If we can eliminate the worker restarts, headroom won't trigger and these transient 429s should disappear.

maya: Perfect. Closing the customer loop now, will update thread with their acceptance of mitigation. :thumbsup:
